headline: Islamabad High Court directs Senate chairman’s adviser to settle dispute with bank by Dec 2
description: Case involves the adviser's conviction for defrauding the financial institution of Rs71 million.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday directed Mian Khurram Rasool, adviser to the Senate chairman, to settle his financial dispute with a bank by December 2 in a case involving his conviction for defrauding the financial institution of Rs71 million.

A division bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Mohammad Sarfraz Dogar issued the direction while hearing an appeal filed by Mr Rasool against his conviction in the bank fraud case.

An accountability court had sentenced him to nine years in prison with a fine of Rs50 million in November 2018 after convicting him of defrauding the private bank of Rs71 million.

During Monday’s hearing, defence counsel Amjad Iqbal Qureshi argued that not a single prosecution witness had testified against his client and maintained that the case was based on no evidence. He contended that the allegations against Mr Rasool were civil in nature and his client was willing to settle the dispute with the bank. He requested the court to grant him some time to resolve the matter.

However, NAB senior prosecutor Rafay Maqsood opposed the request, pointing out that the convict had been seeking time on the same pretext for more than a year but had failed to clear the bank’s outstanding liability.

The chief justice directed Mr Rasool to settle the matter with the bank by December 2.

According to the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), it had filed references against Mr Rasool in 2009, accusing him of fraudulently obtaining loans from a private bank and subsequently defaulting on the amount. The prosecution maintained that Mr Rasool had obtained loans of Rs71 million, Rs10.2 million and Rs10 million from the bank, which later declared him a defaulter on the Rs71 million facility.

Mr Rasool, who previously served as media coordinator to former prime minister Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani, was accused of defrauding financial institutions and members of the public while portraying himself as an adviser to the then prime minister. He is currently serving as media adviser to the Senate chairman.

In a separate allegation mentioned in the NAB proceedings which are pending before another bench of the IHC, Mr Rasool and his brother Shahid Mehmood were accused of inducing members of the public to purchase sugar and scrap from the Trading Corporation of Pakistan and Pakistan Arab Refinery Company and opening fake accounts in the bank with these companies abbreviations, respectively, causing an alleged loss of Rs380 million.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Australian central bank lifts key interest rate to 18-year high
description: Australia’s central bank raised its key interest rate to a 18-year high, citing the prolonged war in the Middle East...
article_text:
Australia’s central bank raised its key interest rate to a 18-year high, citing the prolonged war in the Middle East and persistent inflationary pressures.

In a statement, the Reserve Bank of Australia said it would lift its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85 percent.

“Inflation remains elevated,” it said. “This partly reflects higher fuel and other commodity prices affected by the conflict in the Middle East.”

“AI-related investment is driving rapid growth in prices for technology-related goods, and inflation in many goods and services remains high.”

The hike is the fifth this year, adding to cost-of-living pressures felt by households by increasing home mortgage payments, a politically potent topic in Australia.

headline: Residents seek PM’s intervention over Roshan Pakistan Housing Scheme
description: ISLAMABAD: Residents of Roshan Pakistan (RP) Housing Scheme have approached Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, seeking...
author: Kashif Abbasi, Malik Asad
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: Residents of Roshan Pakistan (RP) Housing Scheme have approached Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, seeking his intervention against the scheme’s management, which they accuse of financial exploitation and intimidation.

A large number of residents have written to the prime minister, requesting action against the management of RP Housing Scheme in Sector E-16 over alleged regulatory violations, financial fraud and harassment.

“We, the undersigned, on behalf of over 2,000 residents, house and plot owners of the RP Housing Scheme, Sector E-16, Islamabad, write to bring to your urgent attention a situation of severe regulatory violations, financial exploitation and gross negligence by the developer, RP Corporation (Pvt) Ltd,” the letter stated.

It added, “As citizens of the capital, we seek your intervention in an issue of pressing nature to uphold the law and protect our fundamental rights. For nearly two decades, we have been trapped in a cycle of uncertainty and exploitation.”

The residents said the scheme was launched in 2004 with a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) and an approved Layout Plan (LOP) from the Capital Development Authority (CDA). However, they said, the CDA suspended the NOC and LOP in 2017 because of the developer’s alleged persistent negligence and failure to meet regulatory commitments.

“Instead of rectifying its failures, the developer has abandoned its obligations, reducing a planned sector to the state of an unmanaged rural settlement. For over a decade, residents have been left without the most basic civic amenities, including paved roads, street lights, water and gas pipelines, a sewerage system, public parks, schools, hospitals and a functional security system,” the letter said.

The residents further alleged that RP Corporation had launched a campaign of financial extortion and intimidation against them.

They said the developer had issued notices (Ref: RPHS/DEV/2026/08), demanding “re-development charges” ranging from Rs250,000 to Rs800,000 per plot.

They termed the demand financial fraud, arguing that the basic infrastructure for which the charges were being collected had never been developed.

They also accused the developer of unlawfully assuming building-control functions by conducting unauthorised inspections, saying such powers rested exclusively with the CDA under the CDA Ordinance, 1960.

They maintained that the suspension of the scheme’s NOC and LOP had rendered the developer’s authority to conduct such inspections invalid.

The residents alleged that the developer was lodging false police complaints against peaceful residents, including accusations of obstruction and threats, to force compliance and silence dissent.

They further claimed that substantial amounts collected from residents as government taxes during plot transfers had reportedly not been deposited with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), indicating possible misappropriation of public funds.

The letter also alleged that the management had withdrawn security arrangements, leading to an increase in theft, robbery and burglary incidents.

It cited Sections 46 and 46-B of the CDA Ordinance, 1960, alleging that re-development charges and inspection fees had been imposed without approval.

It also referred to Clauses 10 and 21 of the Modalities and Procedures (2020), claiming that the developer had failed to complete development work and that the latter clause empowered the CDA to take control of the scheme.

Describing themselves as mostly lower-middle-class families and government employees who had invested their life savings in their homes, the residents said they were being penalised for the regulatory failures of both the developer and the authority.

They asked the prime minister to declare the notice dated Aug 26, 2026, imposing re-development charges, illegal and void; restrain the developer from conducting unauthorised inspections, imposing penalties and collecting charges; and direct the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) to conduct a comprehensive audit of the scheme’s development status and the developer’s accounts, particularly the alleged missing FBR tax revenue.

They also sought protection from what they described as malicious police complaints and urged the CDA to invoke Clause 21 of the 2020 procedures to take control of the scheme.

They proposed that bank guarantees or mortgaged plots be used to complete development work if the developer failed to fulfil its obligations.

The residents further requested a clear roadmap for conditional restoration of the NOC, linked to the provision of basic amenities and infrastructure.

They urged the CDA to fulfil its regulatory role instead of remaining a passive spectator.

When contacted, the society’s spokesman, Ali Hussain, denied the allegations levelled by the allottees.

He told Dawn that possession of plots had been handed over to allottees in 2012 and that they had not been asked to pay any charges since then.

“The society provided them with all facilities, including security, water and road infrastructure,” he said, adding that the management was now reconstructing dilapidated roads and residents would have to share the development cost.

He said the society had taken up the cancellation of its NOC with the CDA and the issue would be resolved soon.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

ISLAMABAD: Residents of Roshan Pakistan (RP) Housing Scheme have approached Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, seeking his intervention against the scheme’s management, which they accuse of financial exploitation and intimidation.

A large number of residents have written to the prime minister, requesting action against the management of RP Housing Scheme in Sector E-16 over alleged regulatory violations, financial fraud and harassment.

“We, the undersigned, on behalf of over 2,000 residents, house and plot owners of the RP Housing Scheme, Sector E-16, Islamabad, write to bring to your urgent attention a situation of severe regulatory violations, financial exploitation and gross negligence by the developer, RP Corporation (Pvt) Ltd,” the letter stated.

It added, “As citizens of the capital, we seek your intervention in an issue of pressing nature to uphold the law and protect our fundamental rights. For nearly two decades, we have been trapped in a cycle of uncertainty and exploitation.”

The residents said the scheme was launched in 2004 with a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) and an approved Layout Plan (LOP) from the Capital Development Authority (CDA). However, they said, the CDA suspended the NOC and LOP in 2017 because of the developer’s alleged persistent negligence and failure to meet regulatory commitments.

“Instead of rectifying its failures, the developer has abandoned its obligations, reducing a planned sector to the state of an unmanaged rural settlement. For over a decade, residents have been left without the most basic civic amenities, including paved roads, street lights, water and gas pipelines, a sewerage system, public parks, schools, hospitals and a functional security system,” the letter said.

The residents further alleged that RP Corporation had launched a campaign of financial extortion and intimidation against them.

They said the developer had issued notices (Ref: RPHS/DEV/2026/08), demanding “re-development charges” ranging from Rs250,000 to Rs800,000 per plot.

They termed the demand financial fraud, arguing that the basic infrastructure for which the charges were being collected had never been developed.

They also accused the developer of unlawfully assuming building-control functions by conducting unauthorised inspections, saying such powers rested exclusively with the CDA under the CDA Ordinance, 1960.

They maintained that the suspension of the scheme’s NOC and LOP had rendered the developer’s authority to conduct such inspections invalid.

The residents alleged that the developer was lodging false police complaints against peaceful residents, including accusations of obstruction and threats, to force compliance and silence dissent.

They further claimed that substantial amounts collected from residents as government taxes during plot transfers had reportedly not been deposited with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), indicating possible misappropriation of public funds.

The letter also alleged that the management had withdrawn security arrangements, leading to an increase in theft, robbery and burglary incidents.

It cited Sections 46 and 46-B of the CDA Ordinance, 1960, alleging that re-development charges and inspection fees had been imposed without approval.

It also referred to Clauses 10 and 21 of the Modalities and Procedures (2020), claiming that the developer had failed to complete development work and that the latter clause empowered the CDA to take control of the scheme.

Describing themselves as mostly lower-middle-class families and government employees who had invested their life savings in their homes, the residents said they were being penalised for the regulatory failures of both the developer and the authority.

They asked the prime minister to declare the notice dated Aug 26, 2026, imposing re-development charges, illegal and void; restrain the developer from conducting unauthorised inspections, imposing penalties and collecting charges; and direct the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) to conduct a comprehensive audit of the scheme’s development status and the developer’s accounts, particularly the alleged missing FBR tax revenue.

They also sought protection from what they described as malicious police complaints and urged the CDA to invoke Clause 21 of the 2020 procedures to take control of the scheme.

They proposed that bank guarantees or mortgaged plots be used to complete development work if the developer failed to fulfil its obligations.

The residents further requested a clear roadmap for conditional restoration of the NOC, linked to the provision of basic amenities and infrastructure.

They urged the CDA to fulfil its regulatory role instead of remaining a passive spectator.

When contacted, the society’s spokesman, Ali Hussain, denied the allegations levelled by the allottees.

He told Dawn that possession of plots had been handed over to allottees in 2012 and that they had not been asked to pay any charges since then.

“The society provided them with all facilities, including security, water and road infrastructure,” he said, adding that the management was now reconstructing dilapidated roads and residents would have to share the development cost.

He said the society had taken up the cancellation of its NOC with the CDA and the issue would be resolved soon.

headline: Two DPOs transferred over poor performance
description: The two DPOs were marked as low performers in a meeting chaired by CM Maryam Nawaz held two weeks back.
author: Asif Chaudhry
article_text:
LAHORE: The Punjab government removed two district police officers (DPO) from their positions over poor performance and reshuffled three BPS-21 officers.

The two DPOs were marked as low performers in a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz held two weeks back where she had expressed displeasure at the 15 DPOs and four RPOs.

Inspector General of Police Punjab Abdul Kareem issued a notification on Monday, removing Chakwal DPO Kashif Zulfiqar and Bhakkar DPO Shahzad Rafique Awan from their positions.

Mr Zulfiqar was directed to report to the Central Police Office (CPO) for further order while Mr Rafique was posted as SP Security Special Branch, Lahore. Both these officers have been replaced by Muhammad Asim and Shahid Ahmad Khan, respectively.

In a separate move, the Punjab government transferred Additional IG South Punjab Kamran Khan and posted him as additional IG Punjab Highways Patrol (PHP) against a vacancy. He was replaced by BPS-21 officer Shahzada Sultan who was earlier serving as additional IG Investigation Punjab.

Additional IG Khurram Ali Shah, awaiting posting, has been posted as additional IG Investigation.

An official who was privy to the development said this individual transfer was interesting as Mr Khurram had earlier served as DG NCCIA. The federal government had transferred him from the post of and posted him as DG Police Bureau. However, he didn’t join the new posting because he was exploring some other assignments. The IGP offered him a position in Punjab.

The official said that Additional IG South Punjab Kamran Khan had served for three years and was willing to get any other assignment. Consequently, the government decided to replace him with Shahzada Sultan to make a move to facilitate Khurram Ali Shah as additional IG Investigation Punjab.

About the transfer of two DPOs, the official said the IGP had issued instructions that the DPOs who were given a grace period to improve crime against women and children would have to meet the targets to prevent their transfers in two weeks or so.The police chief had said that he would review the DPOs performance every week to decide their future.

The official said another review meeting was expected in days to come.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Azma retorts as Salik remembers Parvez Elahi as ‘the best-ever CM’ in Punjab
description: PML-Q leader has also accused Punjab govt of discriminatory spending of public funds in districts.
author: Zulqernain Tahir
article_text:
LAHORE: The remarks by Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain declaring former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Parvez Elahi as the province’s “best-ever chief minister” and his criticism of “unjust” distribution of development funds among the districts have caused unease within the Maryam Nawaz administration, drawing a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised the PML-Q leader not to “bite the hand that feeds him.”

During a private television channel talk show on Monday, Salik lavished praise on Elahi, the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) president, crediting his 2002-07 tenure as Punjab chief executive with delivering development across the province without political or personal bias.

“Former chief minister Chaudhry Parvez Elahi is the best-ever chief executive of Punjab,” he said, adding that Elahi had made a significant contribution to the province’s development and ensured that development initiatives were not dictated by political affiliations.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote. While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of the Maryam Nawaz cabinet in Punjab.

PML-Q leader had also accused Punjab govt of discriminatory spending of public funds in districts

Salik went beyond praising Elahi, and took a swipe at the present provincial administration, alleging that political considerations are increasingly shaping development priorities and influencing the allocation of public funds.

He said he regularly heard complaints of corruption in Punjab, alleging that a disproportionate share of the province’s development budget was being channelled towards Lahore, while districts, like Gujrat, where government-backed candidates failed to win elections, were being sidelined in development planning.

He also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

The criticism drew an immediate response from Punjab information minister Azma Bokhari, who sought to portray Salik’s outburst as a reaction to the denial of a personal favour, rather than a principled objection to the government’s policy.

She alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request for appointment of a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

“Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz does not appoint deputy commissioners at anyone’s recommendation. She makes decisions strictly on merit and in accordance with the government’s policy,” Bokhari said.

Claiming that the chief minister had dismantled the culture of political patronage, personal preferences and recommendations, she maintained that there was no longer any space in Punjab for influential individuals seeking to secure government positions or administrative favours through political connections.

“There is no room for land grabbers and strongmen in Punjab anymore. The practice of rewarding employees of political estates with government positions through recommendations has also come to an end. Salik Hussain should not bite the hand that feeds him,” she retorted.

Rejecting Salik’s allegations of discriminatory development spending, Bokhari said Maryam Nawaz had ensured a transparent and equitable distribution of provincial resources, with development projects of a similar nature being launched in cities across Punjab.

She also claimed that the sanitation model introduced in Lahore had been extended to rural areas, arguing that Punjab government was pursuing development beyond the provincial capital, rather than concentrating resources in one city.

Responding to Salik’s criticism of official aircraft use, Bokhari said Ms Nawaz was the first Punjab chief minister to personally pay expenses incurred on the use of the government’s aeroplane.

She also cited an allocation of Rs12 billion for development in Gujrat, describing it as an unprecedented investment in the city’s history.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

article_html:
LAHORE: The remarks by Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain declaring former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Parvez Elahi as the province’s “best-ever chief minister” and his criticism of “unjust” distribution of development funds among the districts have caused unease within the Maryam Nawaz administration, drawing a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised the PML-Q leader not to “bite the hand that feeds him.”

During a private television channel talk show on Monday, Salik lavished praise on Elahi, the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) president, crediting his 2002-07 tenure as Punjab chief executive with delivering development across the province without political or personal bias.

“Former chief minister Chaudhry Parvez Elahi is the best-ever chief executive of Punjab,” he said, adding that Elahi had made a significant contribution to the province’s development and ensured that development initiatives were not dictated by political affiliations.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote. While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of the Maryam Nawaz cabinet in Punjab.

PML-Q leader had also accused Punjab govt of discriminatory spending of public funds in districts

Salik went beyond praising Elahi, and took a swipe at the present provincial administration, alleging that political considerations are increasingly shaping development priorities and influencing the allocation of public funds.

He said he regularly heard complaints of corruption in Punjab, alleging that a disproportionate share of the province’s development budget was being channelled towards Lahore, while districts, like Gujrat, where government-backed candidates failed to win elections, were being sidelined in development planning.

He also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

The criticism drew an immediate response from Punjab information minister Azma Bokhari, who sought to portray Salik’s outburst as a reaction to the denial of a personal favour, rather than a principled objection to the government’s policy.

She alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request for appointment of a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

“Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz does not appoint deputy commissioners at anyone’s recommendation. She makes decisions strictly on merit and in accordance with the government’s policy,” Bokhari said.

Claiming that the chief minister had dismantled the culture of political patronage, personal preferences and recommendations, she maintained that there was no longer any space in Punjab for influential individuals seeking to secure government positions or administrative favours through political connections.

“There is no room for land grabbers and strongmen in Punjab anymore. The practice of rewarding employees of political estates with government positions through recommendations has also come to an end. Salik Hussain should not bite the hand that feeds him,” she retorted.

Rejecting Salik’s allegations of discriminatory development spending, Bokhari said Maryam Nawaz had ensured a transparent and equitable distribution of provincial resources, with development projects of a similar nature being launched in cities across Punjab.

She also claimed that the sanitation model introduced in Lahore had been extended to rural areas, arguing that Punjab government was pursuing development beyond the provincial capital, rather than concentrating resources in one city.

Responding to Salik’s criticism of official aircraft use, Bokhari said Ms Nawaz was the first Punjab chief minister to personally pay expenses incurred on the use of the government’s aeroplane.

She also cited an allocation of Rs12 billion for development in Gujrat, describing it as an unprecedented investment in the city’s history.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Centre mulls reversing Fata merger, says Fazl
description: Complains character assassination drives launched against him.
author: Manzoor Ali
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman on Monday alleged that the federal government was considering reversing the merger of Fata with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“The merger of Fata with this province is being proposed to be revoked. High-level government men have directly told me that the decision to merge the region was a mistake. Those running this system have told me directly that they want to revoke the merger and restore its previous status,” Mr Fazl told a convention of digital media workers of his party’s merged areas chapter here.

The JUI-F chief said the merged districts had, unfortunately, been made a laboratory.

He added that as a son of the soil and a Pakistani, he had questions that needed to be answered by the government.

Complains character assassination drives launched against him

Mr Fazl, however, said instead of addressing those concerns, character assassination campaigns were launched against him.

“We’re aware of whose behest Fata was merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and whose interests would be served by bringing the area back under federal control,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said that at the time of the merger when the region’s political and constitutional future was being decided, he had expressed serious reservations, maintaining that conditions were not suitable.

He, however, said that even 10 years after the merger, the administrative system of the settled areas had yet to be established in the region.

Mr Fazl said there was still no patwari in the region and the government had failed to establish a land revenue system.

He added that a proper police system couldn’t be set up in the province, while the deputy commissioners posted to the region were baffled and helpless, wondering what to do.

“Today, the issue is not political or constitutional. It’s about Fata’s resources and its economy,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said he had been maintaining for a long time that the issue concerning erstwhile Fata was linked to its mineral resources.

He, however, said he was not opposed to foreign investment by multinational companies.

Mr Fazl said Chinese investors, who were making huge investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), were unhappy as hurdles were being created in the way of their investments.

“If China is not happy about its investment here, other countries, too, would not invest,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said the US was replacing the Chinese.

He said the governor’s rule and an emergency had been imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on the pretext that the provincial government was siding with the terrorist narrative.

Mr Fazl said that after the imposition of governor’s rule, nobody was talking about terrorism and everyone was discussing mineral resources.

He said that for the imposition of the governor’s rule in a province, the governor had to write to the president but no such letter had been written.

“The cabinet’s decision was turned into a summary and shared with the president, which is against legal and constitutional procedures,” he said.

The JUI-F chief insisted that the president was required to state in writing that he agreed with the assertion that the civilian government had broken down, but no such written statement existed in that case.

He also wondered why two systems had been introduced in the province, with one part placed under the governor’s rule and the other under an emergency.

Mr Fazl claimed that Kohat division was also being included in the designated districts.

He said that after he raised his voice, he had become a target of character assassination campaigns, with mainstream and social media being used against him.

The JUI-F chief, however, said he had been facing such campaigns since the 1990s and would not be intimidated by such tactics.

“Today, silence rules the political arena as everyone is silent but only we [JUI-F] are raising our voices,” he said.

Mr Fazl said another narrative was being promoted, accusing the JUI-F of having a soft corner for militants.

“You should be ashamed of saying this as the JUI-F is playing a pivotal role in opposing armed struggle among people,” he said. He said such archaic tactics would not intimidate them.

“If you want a fight, just dare to lay a hand on us and then you will witness the lengths to which our workers will go,” he said.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

PESHAWAR: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman on Monday alleged that the federal government was considering reversing the merger of Fata with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“The merger of Fata with this province is being proposed to be revoked. High-level government men have directly told me that the decision to merge the region was a mistake. Those running this system have told me directly that they want to revoke the merger and restore its previous status,” Mr Fazl told a convention of digital media workers of his party’s merged areas chapter here.

The JUI-F chief said the merged districts had, unfortunately, been made a laboratory.

He added that as a son of the soil and a Pakistani, he had questions that needed to be answered by the government.

Complains character assassination drives launched against him

Mr Fazl, however, said instead of addressing those concerns, character assassination campaigns were launched against him.

“We’re aware of whose behest Fata was merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and whose interests would be served by bringing the area back under federal control,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said that at the time of the merger when the region’s political and constitutional future was being decided, he had expressed serious reservations, maintaining that conditions were not suitable.

He, however, said that even 10 years after the merger, the administrative system of the settled areas had yet to be established in the region.

Mr Fazl said there was still no patwari in the region and the government had failed to establish a land revenue system.

He added that a proper police system couldn’t be set up in the province, while the deputy commissioners posted to the region were baffled and helpless, wondering what to do.

“Today, the issue is not political or constitutional. It’s about Fata’s resources and its economy,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said he had been maintaining for a long time that the issue concerning erstwhile Fata was linked to its mineral resources.

He, however, said he was not opposed to foreign investment by multinational companies.

Mr Fazl said Chinese investors, who were making huge investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), were unhappy as hurdles were being created in the way of their investments.

“If China is not happy about its investment here, other countries, too, would not invest,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said the US was replacing the Chinese.

He said the governor’s rule and an emergency had been imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on the pretext that the provincial government was siding with the terrorist narrative.

Mr Fazl said that after the imposition of governor’s rule, nobody was talking about terrorism and everyone was discussing mineral resources.

He said that for the imposition of the governor’s rule in a province, the governor had to write to the president but no such letter had been written.

“The cabinet’s decision was turned into a summary and shared with the president, which is against legal and constitutional procedures,” he said.

The JUI-F chief insisted that the president was required to state in writing that he agreed with the assertion that the civilian government had broken down, but no such written statement existed in that case.

He also wondered why two systems had been introduced in the province, with one part placed under the governor’s rule and the other under an emergency.

Mr Fazl claimed that Kohat division was also being included in the designated districts.

He said that after he raised his voice, he had become a target of character assassination campaigns, with mainstream and social media being used against him.

The JUI-F chief, however, said he had been facing such campaigns since the 1990s and would not be intimidated by such tactics.

“Today, silence rules the political arena as everyone is silent but only we [JUI-F] are raising our voices,” he said.

Mr Fazl said another narrative was being promoted, accusing the JUI-F of having a soft corner for militants.

“You should be ashamed of saying this as the JUI-F is playing a pivotal role in opposing armed struggle among people,” he said. He said such archaic tactics would not intimidate them.

“If you want a fight, just dare to lay a hand on us and then you will witness the lengths to which our workers will go,” he said.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Kidnapping, firing: Key suspect linked to Gujrat ‘students gang’ held
description: Suspect is allegedly linked to a violent students gang involved in shooting incidents and kidnapping students from different colleges in the city.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
GUJRAT: Police on Monday claimed to have arrested the key suspect allegedly linked to a violent students gang involved in shooting incidents and kidnapping students from different colleges in the city.

A Gujrat police spokesman said on the directions of District Police Officer Faisal Shahzad, Saddar Station House Officer Raja Shehroz raided a place and arrested Amanullah of Gurali, who was allegedly heading a student gang. The suspect was wanted in a case involving the shooting and injuring of a student a few days ago.

He added that Amanullah had also been nominated as a suspect in another kidnapping case registered with the city’s B-Division police station and had been absconding.

The spokesman said Gujrat police were determined to eliminate hooliganism and violence by such gangs from educational institutions and other parts of the city. Meanwhile, Saddar police claimed to have solved the murder of a citizen and arrested three suspects.

Police said the body of Asad Shah, a resident of Moinuddinpur, had been found in a storm water drain on the outskirts of the city. A murder case was registered on Sept 17.

The police said they traced and arrested three suspects, who allegedly confessed to killing Asad through physical torture following an altercation.

Police also claimed to have busted two gangs of robbers and thieves and recovered looted goods and vehicles from their possession.

ACCIDENT: At least five girl students of a school and a rickshaw driver were injured during a road accident along Gujranwala road in Hafizabad city early on Monday.

Rescue officials said a rickshaw carrying students was on its way to the school when a speeding car hit it leaving the rickshaw driver and five girls injured. The injured were shifted to Hafizabad district headquarter hospital where doctors later referred two of them to Lahore.

Hafizabad Deputy Commissioner Syed Hussain Bahadar also reached the hospital and inquired after them and directed the hospital administration to provide better services to the injured.

headline: FIA launches probe into wheat bags theft from Passco stores in Hafizabad
description: Inquiry was initiated after the Passco managing director formally referred the matter to the FIA director general.
author: Waseem Ashraf Butt
article_text:
GUJRAT: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has launched an inquiry into the alleged theft of thousands of wheat bags from the stores of Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (Passco) in Hafizabad.

Official sources said the inquiry was initiated after the Passco managing director formally referred the matter to the FIA director general, following an initial probe that detected shortages and irregularities in the wheat stocks. The sources said seven senior officials of Hafizabad Passco zone, including the zonal head and project manager, went into hiding after the wheat bags theft was surfaced.

The Passco managing director has constituted a special audit inspection committee to comprehensively examine the stocks and scrutinise official documents. The FIA Gujranwala zonal director has been assigned to head the inquiry, and a team has started working in this regard.

Sources said an initial probe by the Passco headquarters and the FIA found that 50,000 wheat bags were missing from the stocks. They said the investigation is expected to identify the suspects involved in the scam.

The investigation team will also assess the financial loss caused to the national exchequer.

According to sources in FIA, a criminal case may be lodged against those found involved in the scam.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

The Passco managing director has constituted a special audit inspection committee to comprehensively examine the stocks and scrutinise official documents. The FIA Gujranwala zonal director has been assigned to head the inquiry, and a team has started working in this regard.

Sources said an initial probe by the Passco headquarters and the FIA found that 50,000 wheat bags were missing from the stocks. They said the investigation is expected to identify the suspects involved in the scam.
The investigation team will also assess the financial loss caused to the national exchequer.
According to sources in FIA, a criminal case may be lodged against those found involved in the scam.

headline: Karachi mayor, opposition trade barbs over pace and quality of development work
description: Wahab says KMC has launched uplift schemes worth billions of rupees using its own resources.
author: Imran Ayub
article_text:
• Wahab says KMC has launched uplift schemes worth billions of rupees using its own resources • Asks TMCs to stop making excuses about limited powers, funds • City Council’s opposition leader questions quality of major infrastructure projects, seeks audit of development funds and details of incomplete projects

KARACHI: A war of words over the city’s development erupted between the mayor and the opposition on Monday, with Mayor Murtaza Wahab claiming that development work had resumed across all seven districts after years of neglect, while Opposition Leader in the City Council Advocate Saifuddin questioned the quality, transparency and pace of the projects, demanding a detailed account of development funds and incomplete schemes.

Addressing a press conference, the mayor said the city was witnessing development without political discrimination, citing ongoing road, water, sewerage, healthcare, sanitation and infrastructure projects.

He said the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) was spending billions of rupees from its own resources and urged town municipal corporations (TMCs), especially controlled by the opposition Jamaat-i-Islami and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf, to work alongside the city government rather than make excuses about limited powers and funds.

However, Advocate Saifuddin rejected the mayor’s claims regarding the development projects and said residents were facing difficulties because of poor-quality work in various towns.

Calling for accountability within his own party’s jurisdictions, he asked the mayor for an audit of development funds allocated to the TMCs that come under JI. He then questioned how many KMC Annual Development Programme (ADP) schemes had been completed and how many remained unfinished despite payments.

The opposition leader also raised questions about the construction quality of major projects, including the Hub Canal and the water supply pipeline in Lyari, while calling for accountability over public spending.

The mayor’s claims

Addressing the press conference at the KMC headquarters, the mayor said his corporation had announced a development budget of Rs68 billion to Rs70bn for the current financial year, adding that projects worth billions of rupees were underway across Karachi.

He said the KMC was carrying out several major schemes from its own resources, including the Chakor Nullah Expressway, being built at a cost of around Rs1bn and the rehabilitation of approximately 140 roads at an estimated cost of Rs13bn.

He said the expressway project was nearing completion and would significantly reduce travel time for commuters heading towards Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The project was expected to open within 30 to 35 days.

A further Rs1bn was being spent on replacing streetlights along 41 major roads, while a new flyover on Garden Nishtar Road, also costing around Rs1bn, was expected to be completed within 100 days.

On water supply, the mayor said the 10-million-gallon-per-day K-III elevated water pipeline for Lyari had been completed and would undergo testing within seven to eight days.

The mayor said the new block of Abbasi Shaheed Hospital covering 200,000 square feet had been completed, with outpatient services expected to begin within the week.

The mayor also announced that three garbage transfer stations were nearing completion and that around Rs30bn was being invested in waste management.

Taking a swipe at critics, Wahab said Karachi’s development was a collective responsibility and urged town administrations to cooperate with the KMC.

“Instead of making excuses about a lack of powers and resources, there is a need for commitment and practical action,” he said, adding that the city government had taken the initiative and development work was now underway across all seven districts.

Opposition’s response

Hardly an hour after the mayor’s presser, the city council opposition leader held a counter press conference at his office, challenging the mayor’s claims, demanding accountability for development spending and questioning the quality of major infrastructure projects.

The opposition leader cited the Hub Canal, reportedly built for Rs12bn, which he claimed developed cracks and suffered damage just three days after its inauguration. He said a section of the canal had reportedly broken even during construction, raising questions about the quality of work and the use of public funds. He also referred to concerns raised by World Bank representatives over safety measures during repair work on the project.

Raising questions about the K-III water pipeline project in Lyari, Mr Saifuddin claimed that a section of the pipeline had collapsed during installation and remained in that condition for a long time, causing difficulties for residents.

He said the authorities must explain the quality of construction and the safeguards adopted in major public projects. public funds. He also referred to concerns raised by World Bank representatives over safety measures during repair work on the project.

Raising questions about the K-III water pipeline project in Lyari, Mr Saifuddin claimed that a section of the pipeline had collapsed during installation and remained in that condition for a long time, causing difficulties for residents.

He said the authorities must explain the quality of construction and the safeguards adopted in major public projects.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: JIT chief issued show cause over delay in submission of final charge sheet in Mir Raza murder case
description: DSP Lashari is no longer IO in the case after formation of JIT, court told.
author: Sumair Abdullah
article_text:
KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Monday issued a show-cause notice to DIG Irfan Baloch, chief of the newly formed joint investigation team (JIT) in the Mir Raza murder case, after police failed to submit the final charge sheet. He has been directed to respond by Nov 10.

The Sindh home department had formed the JIT, led by DIG Baloch, on the recommendation of a single-member judicial commission comprising Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court.

The team was tasked with investigating the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza’s death and possible negligence in the case.

Two previous high-level investigation teams had failed to identify the culprit or establish how Mir Raza’s body came to be found in mysterious circumstances.

DSP Lashari is no longer IO in the case after formation of JIT, court told

The then investigating officers (IOs) had sought three extensions to submit the final report, saying that they were awaiting forensic reports and a response from Apple company regarding Mir Raza’s mobile phone.

Complainant’s counsel Daniyal Muhammad Hussain told Dawn that at Monday’s hearing the complainant’s side informed the court that DSP Sirajuddin Lashari was no longer the IO in the case as a JIT had been formed. He also submitted the official notification regarding the JIT’s formation.

He added that no police official or JIT member appeared before the court, although the date had been fixed for submission of the final charge sheet.

After a brief hearing, the magistrate asked the JIT head to explain why the charge sheet had not been submitted.

DSP Lashari told this reporter that he had handed over the case file to the JIT head so the team could proceed with the investigation, adding that he was no longer the IO.

Mir Raza, 25, a businessman, had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS. His body, bearing a gunshot wound, was found in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day later.

In his interim report, the IO named 63 witnesses but wrote “no one” in the column for the accused. In his conclusion, he stated that despite probing all possible angles, police had yet to find any clue or make a breakthrough.

The report also contained detailed information about the case, from the registration of the FIR on the complaint of Mir Raza’s father after he went missing to the handover of the investigation to the JIT.

article_html:
KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Monday issued a show-cause notice to DIG Irfan Baloch, chief of the newly formed joint investigation team (JIT) in the Mir Raza murder case, after police failed to submit the final charge sheet. He has been directed to respond by Nov 10.

The Sindh home department had formed the JIT, led by DIG Baloch, on the recommendation of a single-member judicial commission comprising Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court.

The team was tasked with investigating the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza’s death and possible negligence in the case.

Two previous high-level investigation teams had failed to identify the culprit or establish how Mir Raza’s body came to be found in mysterious circumstances.

DSP Lashari is no longer IO in the case after formation of JIT, court told

The then investigating officers (IOs) had sought three extensions to submit the final report, saying that they were awaiting forensic reports and a response from Apple company regarding Mir Raza’s mobile phone.

Complainant’s counsel Daniyal Muhammad Hussain told Dawn that at Monday’s hearing the complainant’s side informed the court that DSP Sirajuddin Lashari was no longer the IO in the case as a JIT had been formed. He also submitted the official notification regarding the JIT’s formation.

He added that no police official or JIT member appeared before the court, although the date had been fixed for submission of the final charge sheet.

After a brief hearing, the magistrate asked the JIT head to explain why the charge sheet had not been submitted.

DSP Lashari told this reporter that he had handed over the case file to the JIT head so the team could proceed with the investigation, adding that he was no longer the IO.

Mir Raza, 25, a businessman, had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS. His body, bearing a gunshot wound, was found in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day later.

In his interim report, the IO named 63 witnesses but wrote “no one” in the column for the accused. In his conclusion, he stated that despite probing all possible angles, police had yet to find any clue or make a breakthrough.

The report also contained detailed information about the case, from the registration of the FIR on the complaint of Mir Raza’s father after he went missing to the handover of the investigation to the JIT.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Free-will couple’s plea for protection put off till 23rd
description: The couple has sought a court order for protection from alleged threat to their lives from the wife's family members and other relatives.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
LARKANA: Justice Muhammed Osman Ali Hadi of Sindh High Court’s Larkana bench adjourned a freewill couple’s petition till Nov 23 as the petitioners, seeking protection against alleged threat to their lives, did not appear before him on Monday.

Advocate Mohammad Afzal Jagirani was present in the court to represent the petitioners. A lawyer, Athar Abbas Solangi, who has volunteered to appear in court on behalf of the woman’s father, Sanjay Kumar, was also present.

The couple, Yasir Ali Domki and Yasmeen (as she identified herself in the petition) have sought a court order for protection from alleged threat to their lives from her family members and other relatives.

According to the petition, the woman, Bindya Kumari, contracted a freewill marriage with Yasir Domki on Oct 15, 2026 after embracing Islam and adopted ‘Yasmeen’ as her Islamic name.

The woman’s family members and relatives disbelieved the couple’s claim. The matter was reported to the Sibbi (Balochistan) and Bakhshapur (Sindh) police stations. The complainants, Sanjay Kumar, along with his relatives, demand recovery of his daughter alleging that she had been abducted.

In the petition, Yasmeen stated that she had not been abducted and that she contracted a freewill marriage with Yasir Domki without any duress or pressure.

“We have now been living a happy life with each other,” the couple’s petition stated.

They alleged that the [woman’s] family and other relatives were bent upon getting the marriage undone at any cost for which they were trying to implicate them in false criminal cases.

According to the petition, the couple approached SHOs of the Sibbi and Bakhshapur (Kandhkot-Kashmore district) and later SSPs of the two districts for protection. The police officers, instead, were also threatening them (the petitioners) to surrender else they would be implicated in false criminal cases, the couple alleged.

“We fear for our lives and should be provided police protection,” the petitioners urged.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Sindh CM reviews WB-funded projects worth $3.8bn
description: Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah directs departments and project teams to take ownership of pending actions, strengthen coordination and meet timelines.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Monday reviewed a portfolio of 12 World Bank-financed projects worth $3.849 billion and directed the departments concerned to speed up implementation, resolve bottlenecks and meet agreed timelines so that the investments translate into better public services.

He was chairing a high-level portfolio review meeting with World Bank Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar at CM House to take stock of implementation, financial progress, procurement and outstanding challenges across the province.

According to a statement issued by CM House, the meeting reviewed 12 active operations with a combined commitment of $3.849bn. Of this, $2.334bn has been disbursed and $1.511bn remains undisbursed.

Participants also examined the financial and procurement performance of the projects, including the 2026-27 disbursement target of $381.2m, with a stretch target of $434.2m. Actual disbursements so far stand at $43.2m.

The chief minister directed departments and project teams to take ownership of pending actions, strengthen coordination and meet agreed timelines.

The $240 million Second Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP-2) was reviewed with particular attention to the K-IV associated facilities. The meeting noted that environmental and social instruments for the facilities had been prepared and submitted to the World Bank for clearance, while compliance monitoring was continuing.

The Karachi Mobility Project, which includes the Yellow Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor and associated road infrastructure, was reviewed with particular attention to the Jam Sadiq Bridge and bus depots.

article_html:
KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Monday reviewed a portfolio of 12 World Bank-financed projects worth $3.849 billion and directed the departments concerned to speed up implementation, resolve bottlenecks and meet agreed timelines so that the investments translate into better public services.

He was chairing a high-level portfolio review meeting with World Bank Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar at CM House to take stock of implementation, financial progress, procurement and outstanding challenges across the province.

According to a statement issued by CM House, the meeting reviewed 12 active operations with a combined commitment of $3.849bn. Of this, $2.334bn has been disbursed and $1.511bn remains undisbursed.

Participants also examined the financial and procurement performance of the projects, including the 2026-27 disbursement target of $381.2m, with a stretch target of $434.2m. Actual disbursements so far stand at $43.2m.

The chief minister directed departments and project teams to take ownership of pending actions, strengthen coordination and meet agreed timelines.

The $240 million Second Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP-2) was reviewed with particular attention to the K-IV associated facilities. The meeting noted that environmental and social instruments for the facilities had been prepared and submitted to the World Bank for clearance, while compliance monitoring was continuing.

The Karachi Mobility Project, which includes the Yellow Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor and associated road infrastructure, was reviewed with particular attention to the Jam Sadiq Bridge and bus depots.

Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

headline: Ignite’s National Incubation Centers win prestigious International Award in London
description: Global recognition underscores Pakistan’s growing innovation ecosystem and its commitment to technology-led economic development.
author: ADVERTORIAL
article_text:
Pakistan has earned international recognition for its efforts to advance technology entrepreneurship, with Ignite – National Technology Fund’s National Incubation Centers (NICs) Program winning the Digital Policy & Regulatory Excellence Award at the Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation (CTO) Digital Excellence Awards 2026 in London.

Presented during the CTO’s 125th anniversary celebrations, the award recognises the NIC Program as a significant initiative in fostering innovation, entrepreneurship and digital economic development. Pakistan also secured recognition in two other categories, distinguishing itself among the organisation’s 56 member countries.

The achievement reflects Pakistan’s growing commitment to building an inclusive, sustainable and globally competitive technology ecosystem.

Leadership and Vision

The recognition highlights the strategic leadership of Information Technology & Telecommunication Federal Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja whose focus on digital transformation, entrepreneurship and institutional collaboration has helped reinforce Pakistan’s technology development agenda.

Her emphasis on empowering young innovators, strengthening the startup ecosystem and creating opportunities in the digital economy aligns with Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif’s vision of a digitally empowered Pakistan.

Under the Ministry’s guidance, Ignite has continued to develop the NIC Program as a flagship national initiative, connecting entrepreneurial talent with the resources, expertise and networks needed to establish and scale technology-driven businesses.

The international distinction underscores the importance of sustained policy commitment, effective institutional leadership and public-private collaboration in advancing Pakistan’s digital ambitions.

Transforming innovation into opportunity

Through its nationwide network, the NIC Program provides startups with structured incubation, mentorship, business development support, industry connections and access to potential investors.

By bringing together public investment and private-sector expertise, the program helps bridge the gap between innovative ideas and commercially viable enterprises.

Its contribution extends beyond individual startups. By supporting emerging technologies, encouraging entrepreneurship and expanding access to innovation opportunities, the NIC Program is helping strengthen the foundations of a knowledge-based economy.

The award also recognises the collective efforts of Ignite’s leadership, NIC operators, consortium partners, mentors, investors and entrepreneurs who continue to contribute to Pakistan’s evolving startup ecosystem.

A milestone for Pakistan’s digital future

The CTO recognition is more than an international accolade. It demonstrates how sustained investment in entrepreneurial infrastructure, institutional capacity and innovation can contribute to national economic development.

For Pakistan, the achievement offers an opportunity to build further momentum through stronger industry partnerships, greater investment linkages and continued support for technology entrepreneurs.

As the country pursues its digital transformation agenda, the success of the NIC Program provides an encouraging example of how strategic public-sector initiatives can help unlock private-sector potential.

Ultimately, Pakistan’s technological future will be shaped by the ingenuity of its people and the opportunities created for them to succeed. Ignite’s NIC Program is helping turn that potential into enterprise, innovation and economic opportunity—earning recognition well beyond Pakistan’s borders.

headline: Editorial: There is a brief opportunity for peace with Iran. Flexibility, not US-Israeli force, can secure it
description: AS the threat of renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran lingers, a parallel diplomatic process — facilitated by Qatar...
article_text:
AS the threat of renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran lingers, a parallel diplomatic process — facilitated by Qatar and Pakistan — is attempting to avert a devastating return to hostilities.

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday to take part in indirect talks aimed at working out a deal, even as speculation of fresh attacks on Iran, following today’s midterm polls in America, continued.

US President Donald Trump has not helped matters by toying with the idea of new attacks. The ice was broken late last month when US Vice-President J.D. Vance wrote a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

Mr Vance reportedly prefers a diplomatic solution. Earlier, he had led his country’s delegation during April’s historic talks in Islamabad. The letter has been well received in Tehran, with Gen Rezaei calling its tone “positive”.

headline: US signals progress in Iran talks to avert flare-up
description: A deal with Tehran “could happen”, Trump says on his Truth Social platform.
author: AFP
article_text:
US President Donald Trump signaled progress on Tuesday in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Tehran reported “intensive” exchanges while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.

The fresh diplomatic signals came ahead of US midterm elections on Tuesday, in which Trump’s Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress, faced with voter dissatisfaction over the conflict and the soaring fuel prices it has triggered.

A deal with Tehran “could happen,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

“Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible.”

But hours later, Washington’s diplomatic overtures were dashed by a report that the United States had attacked Iran, in what the Wall Street Journal said was the latest in a string of limited strikes it secretly carried out against the Islamic republic in recent weeks.

Iranian state media reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

Earlier, oil prices plunged by more than seven per cent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict.

The WSJ report came shortly before polls opened in the midterms, in which Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

Reopen the strait

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators.

“Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media.

“Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations.”

Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement.

“We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday.

China also urged a return to diplomacy, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.

Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from Washington were “an acknowledgement of our victory.”

A senior Iranian official said that Tehran was ready to open the Hormuz strait, an export conduit for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days — as long as Washington agreed to its list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait, with demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” Tehran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

Chinese President Xi Jinping also discussed the war with Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday – the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” an Omani statement said.

‘No compromises’

China held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday as well.

Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,” Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard,” state TV reported.

article_html:
US President Donald Trump signaled progress on Tuesday in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Tehran reported “intensive” exchanges while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.

The fresh diplomatic signals came ahead of US midterm elections on Tuesday, in which Trump’s Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress, faced with voter dissatisfaction over the conflict and the soaring fuel prices it has triggered.

A deal with Tehran “could happen,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

“Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible.”

But hours later, Washington’s diplomatic overtures were dashed by a report that the United States had attacked Iran, in what the Wall Street Journal said was the latest in a string of limited strikes it secretly carried out against the Islamic republic in recent weeks.

Iranian state media reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

Earlier, oil prices plunged by more than seven per cent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict.

The WSJ report came shortly before polls opened in the midterms, in which Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

Reopen the strait

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators.

“Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media.

“Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations.”

Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement.

“We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday.

China also urged a return to diplomacy, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.

Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from Washington were “an acknowledgement of our victory.”

A senior Iranian official said that Tehran was ready to open the Hormuz strait, an export conduit for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days — as long as Washington agreed to its list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait, with demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” Tehran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

Chinese President Xi Jinping also discussed the war with Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday – the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” an Omani statement said.

‘No compromises’

China held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday as well.

Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,” Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard,” state TV reported.

In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.

He said Washington must also remove sanctions imposed recently and reduce American troop numbers in the region.

Trump has kept up his threats against Tehran, saying on Sunday that the United States may have to give Iran “the hammer” at some unspecified time.

On Saturday, the US leader said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

Baqaei warned that any act of aggression against Iran “will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response. “

headline: Donald the Lame Duck? Trump will have other ideas if Republicans lose midterms
description: Analysts warn that Trump as a “lame duck” president could be the most vengeful Trump of all.
author: AFP
article_text:
President Donald Trump’s second term has been a wild ride, but his last two years in power could be wilder still if Republicans lose control of Congress in Tuesday’s US midterm elections.

From renewed military action against Iran to election challenges and fightbacks against Democratic investigations, Trump’s post-midterms playbook could involve disruption on all fronts.

Analysts warn that Trump as a “lame duck” president could be the most vengeful Trump of all.

“I’m skeptical that President Trump will go quiet into that good night,” Peter Loge, director of George Washington University’s School of Media and Public Affairs, told AFP.

“There is nothing in history that says he will say ‘I’ve been beaten, my time is over’. Every time Trump has been backed into a corner, he has shouted more and come out fighting.”

Vetoes and vengeance

Trump has always viewed himself as a fighter. He has been clear he will take the same approach if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress.

“If we didn’t win, I veto everything” in any Democratic legislative agenda, Trump told the New York Post.

The White House says it is also ready to fight back against whatever investigations — or impeachment proceedings — Democrats throw at them.

“They’ll probably go after me, and I’ll go after them,” Trump said in a Time magazine interview. Trump could even direct the Justice Department to investigate Democrats who are probing him.

Trump, who baselessly disputed his 2020 presidential election loss, could also interfere in the midterms by challenging counts or delaying the certification of disputed races.

Iran

Foreign policy is the one area in which lame-duck US presidents still have wide-ranging powers.

Trump may renew large-scale military operations against Iran, although he appeared to indicate on the eve of the midterms that fresh talks could produce a deal.

“I don’t think he wants his legacy to be a warmonger. He wants his legacy to have left America stronger,” Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP.

Speculation has swirled that Trump could fire Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth as the Iran war drags on — a familiar move for a president who never likes to take the blame.

Ukraine, detente and trade

Trump loves to think of himself as a master of peace deals and is likely to continue to push Ukraine to agree to a settlement with Russia. Fresh trilateral talks are set for next week.

At the same time, Trump will continue to seek detente with the leaders he views as his great power equals — Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The three will potentially meet at a summit in China later this month.

The US is also likely to continue its retrenchment from some of its NATO and other Western allies — and may even accelerate it, said Hass of the Brookings Institution.

On trade, however, Trump would likely remain “unrelentingly active”, as shown by his recent hostility towards Canada, Hass said.

Staying relevant for 2028?

Trump loves being the centre of attention and is unlikely to relish the spotlight turning towards potential successors in the 2028 US presidential election.

Trump — who hosted the reality television show The Apprentice — has been notably coy about backing either Vice President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio for the top job.

But Trump has largely stopped dropping hints at running for a constitutionally-barred third term.

Allan Lichtman, a professor at American University and author of Great American Presidents: The Twelve Who Transformed the Nation, said Trump would certainly “keep the focus on himself by being the kingmaker.”

Monuments to himself

Like other people getting ready for retirement, Trump may choose to focus on home improvement.

In his closing midterms speech, Trump barely mentioned policy and instead talked about his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other plans to beautify Washington.

Trump has openly expressed a desire to stamp his own physical mark on Washington because he fears that others will not do it for him.

“We have a lot of great things planned for Washington,” he said at the Reflecting Pool on Monday.

Header image: US President Donald Trump stands, as he departs after delivering remarks ahead of the midterm elections at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, after being reopened following months of repairs, in Washington, DC, US on Nov 2, 2026. —Reuters
